acceptance.title: 1. Acceptance of these terms
acceptance.body:
By signing up for or using Q Task Manager (the 'Service') you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, do not use the Service.

These terms govern your access to and use of the Service, including any content, functionality, and services offered.

service.title: 2. Description of the service
service.body:
Q Task Manager is a multi-tenant task management platform designed for businesses in Iraq, Kurdistan, and the wider MENA region. The Service includes task creation and assignment, team collaboration, role-based permissions, activity logging, file storage, broadcasts, and reporting.

We may modify or discontinue features with notice. Material changes will be announced in-app and by email to workspace admins.

accounts.title: 3. Your account
accounts.body:
You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your authentication credentials and for all activity under your account. Notify us immediately of any unauthorized use.

A single workspace ('tenant') is owned by the user who creates it. That user becomes the CEO of the workspace and has full administrative authority over invited users.

subscriptions.title: 4. Subscriptions and payment
subscriptions.body:
The Service is offered on a 14-day free trial, after which a paid subscription is required to continue using paid features. Plans are billed monthly or annually.

Payment is processed by our payment providers (Paddle or Stripe). For customers in regions our card providers do not serve, manual bank transfer is available. If payment fails on an active subscription, your workspace enters a graduated read-only / suspended / locked state before deletion at day 120.

acceptableUse.title: 5. Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body:
You agree not to use the Service to: violate any law; infringe intellectual property; transmit malware; harass, defame, or threaten others; spam; reverse-engineer or attempt to bypass security controls; or use the Service to compete with us.

We reserve the right to suspend or terminate accounts engaged in prohibited conduct.

content.title: 6. Your content
content.body:
You retain all rights to the content you upload (tasks, comments, files, etc.). You grant us a limited license to host and process that content solely to provide the Service.

We will not access your content except: (a) to provide and maintain the Service, (b) to comply with legal obligations, or (c) with your express consent.

termination.title: 7. Termination
termination.body:
You may cancel your account at any time from the Billing page or by contacting support. We may suspend or terminate your access for material breach of these terms with notice where reasonably practicable.

On termination, you may export your data for 30 days. After that, data may be deleted.

disclaimer.title: 8. Disclaimer of warranties
disclaimer.body: The Service is provided 'as is' and 'as available.' We disclaim all warranties, express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement, to the maximum extent permitted by law.

liability.title: 9. Limitation of liability
liability.body:
To the maximum extent permitted by law, our total liability for any claim arising out of these terms or the Service is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months preceding the claim.

We are not liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages.

changes.title: 10. Changes to these terms
changes.body: We may update these terms from time to time. Material changes will be announced 30 days in advance via email to workspace admins and an in-app notice. Continued use of the Service after the effective date constitutes acceptance.

contact.title: 11. Contact
contact.body: Questions about these terms? Contact us at legal@qtaskmanager.com or via your in-app support channel.

intro.title: 1. Introduction
intro.body: This Privacy Policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, who we share it with, and your rights. It applies to your use of the Service at qtaskmanager.com and any related applications.

dataCollected.title: 2. Data we collect
dataCollected.body:
Account data: name, email, encrypted password (handled by Clerk; we never see passwords).

Workspace data: tasks, comments, files, broadcasts, activity log entries, role assignments — anything you or your team produce inside the Service.

Profile data (optional): date of birth, address, emergency contact, national ID (encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM), CV, certificates.

Usage data: API request logs, authentication events, error reports (via Sentry).

Device data: IP address, browser user-agent, operating system.

dataUse.title: 3. How we use your data
dataUse.body:
To provide and operate the Service. To authenticate you. To send transactional emails (task notifications, billing receipts). To respond to support requests. To detect, prevent, and address fraud or abuse. To comply with legal obligations.

We do NOT sell your data. We do NOT use your content to train AI models. We do NOT share your workspace data with other tenants.

dataSharing.title: 4. Sharing with third parties
dataSharing.body: We share data only with subprocessors that help us run the Service (see next section), with law enforcement when legally required, or with your explicit consent.

subprocessors.title: 5. Subprocessors
subprocessors.body:
Clerk (authentication, USA). Neon (database, EU). Cloudflare R2 (file storage, EU). Resend (transactional email, EU). Paddle (payments, UK). Stripe (payments, USA). Pusher (real-time, USA). Sentry (error monitoring, EU). PostHog (product analytics, EU).

A current subprocessor list is available on request. We will notify workspace admins 30 days in advance of adding a new subprocessor.

retention.title: 6. Data retention
retention.body:
Workspace data is retained as long as your subscription is active, plus 120 days after final cancellation (during which you can recover or export).

Authentication audit data is retained for 12 months. Activity log entries are retained for the life of the workspace (immutable).

Deletion is permanent on day 120 of the past-due lifecycle unless you recover.

security.title: 7. Security
security.body:
Multi-tenant data isolation enforced at three layers: application code, database row-level security, and tenant-scoped object keys in file storage.

Encryption at rest for sensitive PII (national ID). Encryption in transit (HTTPS) for all third-party connections. Quarterly security audits and an annual penetration test.

Despite our efforts no system is 100% secure. If we become aware of a data breach affecting your data, we will notify you within 72 hours.

rights.title: 8. Your rights
rights.body:
Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have the right to: access the data we hold about you; correct inaccurate data; delete your data; restrict or object to processing; data portability (we provide a one-click ZIP export at /billing).

To exercise these rights, contact privacy@qtaskmanager.com.

cookies.title: 9. Cookies
cookies.body:
We use essential cookies for authentication and security (Clerk session). Analytics cookies (PostHog) only with consent.

No advertising cookies. No third-party tracking pixels.

children.title: 10. Children
children.body: The Service is intended for use by businesses and is not directed to children under 18. We do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 18. If you believe we have, contact us and we will delete it.

changes.title: 11. Changes to this policy
changes.body: Material changes will be announced 30 days in advance by email and in-app notice. The 'Last updated' date at the top of this page reflects the most recent change.

contact.title: 12. Contact
contact.body: Privacy questions: privacy@qtaskmanager.com. For requests under GDPR, CCPA, or similar laws, please include your workspace identifier.

dpa.title: Data Processing Addendum
dpa.meta: Last updated 2026-05-31 · For customers subject to GDPR or equivalent regimes

scope.title: 1. Scope and definitions
scope.body:
This Data Processing Addendum ('DPA') supplements the Terms of Service between you ('Customer') and us ('Processor') and governs our processing of personal data on your behalf.

Terms not defined here have the meanings given in the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) or equivalent local data protection law.

roles.title: 2. Roles of the parties
roles.body:
You are the Data Controller. We are a Data Processor acting on your documented instructions. Our subprocessors are Sub-processors.

Where we process data for our own administrative purposes (e.g. fraud detection, billing), we act as an independent controller of that limited set of data.

processingScope.title: 3. Scope of processing
processingScope.body:
Categories of data subjects: your authorized users (workspace members), and individuals named in tasks, comments, or files within your workspace.

Categories of data: contact details, profile data, employment data, content authored by users.

Purpose: to provide the Service as described in the Terms of Service.

Duration: for the term of your subscription plus the retention windows described in the Privacy Policy.

subprocessors.title: 4. Subprocessors
subprocessors.body: You authorize us to engage subprocessors listed in the Privacy Policy section 5. We will give 30 days' prior notice of any new subprocessor; you may object on reasonable grounds and we will work to find a solution or you may terminate the affected service.

security.title: 5. Security measures
security.body: We implement and maintain technical and organizational measures appropriate to the risk, including: encryption at rest and in transit, multi-layer tenant isolation (application + database RLS + storage), role-based access controls, audit logging, regular vulnerability scanning, and annual penetration testing.

dataSubjectRights.title: 6. Assisting with data subject rights
dataSubjectRights.body:
We provide tools (data export at /billing, account deletion, profile editing) that enable you to respond to access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, and objection requests from your users.

Where these tools are insufficient, we will assist you on request, taking into account the nature of the processing.

breachNotification.title: 7. Personal data breach
breachNotification.body: We will notify you without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting your data. The notice will include: the nature of the breach, categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, consequences, and measures taken or proposed.

transfers.title: 8. International data transfers
transfers.body: Some of our subprocessors are located outside the EEA. Transfers occur under Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 3, Processor-to-Processor) as approved by the European Commission, or under another lawful transfer mechanism.

audit.title: 9. Audit rights
audit.body: On reasonable notice and at your cost, you may audit our compliance with this DPA up to once per year. We may satisfy audit requests by providing recent third-party audit reports (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001 once obtained).

termination.title: 10. Termination and data return
termination.body: On termination of the Service, we will return or delete personal data at your option within 30 days, unless retention is required by law. The ZIP export at /billing is the primary return mechanism.

liability.title: 11. Liability
liability.body: Our liability under this DPA is subject to the same limits as the Terms of Service. Where the GDPR or equivalent law imposes a higher minimum, that minimum applies.

contact.body: Privacy and DPA questions: privacy@qtaskmanager.com. Data Protection Officer: [TO BE APPOINTED].

gettingStarted.title: Getting started with Q Task Manager
gettingStarted.description: From signup to your team's first completed task — about ten minutes end-to-end.

footer.cta: Stuck? <link>Back to the help index</link>, or read the Admin guide for more detail.

signup.title: 1. Sign up and create your workspace
signup.body:
Go to /sign-up and enter your work email and a password. Q Task Manager uses email + password authentication; you'll receive a verification link.

On first sign-in we create a new workspace named after you ('Your Name's Workspace'). You become the CEO of that workspace automatically — every later user you invite joins this workspace under your authority.

The workspace name and slug can be changed later under Company settings.

verifyEmail.title: 2. Verify your email
verifyEmail.body:
Open the verification email we sent and click the link. Until verification is complete you can browse but not invite teammates.

If the email didn't arrive, check spam, then re-trigger from the sign-in screen. Issues persist? Contact support.

orgSetup.title: 3. Set up your org structure (optional)
orgSetup.body:
You start with one Branch ('Main') and one Department ('Executive'). For most small teams that's enough.

If you have multiple locations or departments, head to Administration → Branches and Administration → Departments. Branches contain Departments, Departments contain Teams. Users belong to one Department and any number of Teams.

items.2: Click 'Invite person', enter their email, choose their role.
items.3: Confirm. Q Task Manager sends them an invitation by email.
items.4: They click the link, set a password, and land on their dashboard.

items.1: Open Tasks in the sidebar, click 'New task'.
items.2: Add a title, optional description, due date, and priority.
items.3: Pick an assignee — anyone in your workspace.
items.4: Save. The task lands in their inbox; they accept it.
items.5: When the work is done, they submit; you approve; the task is marked completed.

nextSteps.title: Where to go next
nextSteps.body:
Most workspaces are productive within the first hour. From here:

• Admins (CEO, Admin, HR, Manager): read the Admin guide for billing, broadcasts, exports, and activity log.

• Everyone else: read the Employee guide for tasks, comments, notifications, and your profile.

• Hit the bell icon in the header to see your notifications. Use the language switcher (EN / العربية / کوردی) to change the interface language.

overview.title: Who counts as an admin
overview.body:
Q Task Manager has six built-in org roles: CEO, Admin, Manager, Supervisor, HR, and Employee. The first four can perform admin actions — invite users, approve invitations, create departments — with progressively narrower scope. CEO sees everything in the workspace; HR sees their department; Manager sees the teams they supervise.

If you need finer-grained access, create system roles under Administration → Roles and grant them to specific users.

orgStructure.title: Org structure
orgStructure.body:
Three layers: Branches (locations or business units) → Departments (functional groups within a branch) → Teams (working units within a department).

Users belong to exactly one Department, and any number of Teams. Tasks can be assigned to a single person OR a Team — when assigned to a Team, any member can accept.

Departments can have a parent Department to model nested orgs. The Executive department starts as the root.

invitingUsers.title: Inviting users
invitingUsers.body:
Open People → Invite person. Fill in name, email, role, branch, department. CEO and Admin invites are sent immediately. Manager / Supervisor invites go through an approval chain (configurable under Company settings) before the invitation email goes out.

The plan limit applies: the Starter plan allows 3 paid users (active or invited). You'll see a 422 error if you try to exceed it; upgrade or remove an unused seat first.

rolesPermissions.title: Roles and permissions
rolesPermissions.body:
Administration → Roles shows every role in your workspace, including the six built-in ones. Built-in roles can't be edited; create a copy if you need a variant.

A user's effective permissions are the union of their org role plus any system roles you grant them. The 'Admin' system role unlocks the admin dashboard variant; the 'Manager' system role unlocks the manager dashboard.

Every role change is recorded in the activity log.

departmentsTeams.title: Branches, departments, and teams
departmentsTeams.body:
Administration → Branches lets you add or archive branches. Archiving hides a branch from default lists but preserves history. Branches have a name and optional code.

Administration → Departments shows the department tree. Departments inherit their branch from their parent. Each department can have a manager and supervisors. Department managers see all tasks in their department.

Teams live inside departments. Each team has one supervisor; team members are a subset of the department. Tasks can be assigned to a team — any member can accept.

broadcasts.title: Broadcasts
broadcasts.body:
Broadcasts are fire-and-forget company-wide announcements. Compose at Broadcasts → New broadcast. Pick an audience: everyone, one branch, one role, or a custom list of users.

Every recipient gets an in-app notification and an email (subject to their notification preferences). Broadcasts are NOT real-time chat — they're announcements. There's no reply thread.

activityLog.title: Activity log
activityLog.body:
Open Activity log in the sidebar. The log is immutable — once written, rows cannot be edited or deleted, only viewed.

Filters let you scope by date range, actor, action type, or target. Export as CSV at any time via the export button. CEO and Admin see the full log; Manager / HR see only events scoped to their authority.

billing.title: Billing
billing.body:
Administration → Billing shows your current plan, usage (paid users and storage), trial end date if applicable, and the upgrade button.

Upgrade options depend on your country. If our primary card provider isn't available where you are, we offer a Bank transfer option: we issue an invoice with our bank details, you wire the payment, submit the transfer reference, and our team marks it paid (usually within one business day).

If payment fails on an active subscription, you'll go through a grace period (7 days), then read-only mode (week 2), then suspension (weeks 3–4), then locked (weeks 5–17). Day 120 the workspace is deleted. You can recover by paying at any point in the cascade.

dataExport.title: Data export
dataExport.body:
Administration → Billing → Export company data downloads a ZIP of every table in your workspace, as CSV + JSON pairs. Useful for migration, backups, or compliance.

The link is valid for 7 days; you can re-request a new export at any time.

security.title: Security
security.body:
Q Task Manager is multi-tenant: data is isolated at three levels — application code, database row-level security, and tenant-scoped object keys in file storage.

Personal identifiers (national_id) are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. Other fields (date of birth, address, emergency contact) are stored in plaintext but only visible to the user, their manager, and HR.

Third parties: Clerk handles authentication (we never see passwords); Cloudflare R2 stores file uploads; Resend delivers emails; Paddle/Stripe handle card payments. All connections are HTTPS.

employee.description: Day-to-day Q Task Manager for individual contributors.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.body:
When you sign in, you land on the Home dashboard. It shows five widgets: tasks waiting for you, what's due this week, recent activity, recent comments mentioning you, and a quick-stats summary.

If you have a Manager / Supervisor / HR / Admin role, you'll see an extra 'Manager dashboard' or 'Admin dashboard' option in the sidebar with deeper analytics.

myTasks.title: Your tasks
myTasks.body:
Tasks in the sidebar shows everything assigned to you or your teams, plus tasks you created. Use the status, priority, and date filters to narrow down.

Tasks have a status lifecycle: draft → assigned → in progress → submitted → approved → completed. (Some tasks bounce through 'needs revision' or 'cancelled' along the way.) Your current task's status is shown as a coloured badge.

taskLifecycle.title: Task lifecycle, step by step
taskLifecycle.body:
When a task is assigned to you, it appears in your inbox at status 'assigned'. Open it, read the description, and click Accept to move it to 'in progress'.

When the work is done, click Submit. Optionally attach files or leave a submission note. The task moves to 'submitted'; the task's creator gets a notification to review.

If they approve, the task moves to 'completed'. If they request a revision, the task goes back to 'needs revision' with their comments — make the changes and resubmit.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.body:
Tasks can carry file attachments (PDFs, Office docs, images). Drag-and-drop or click 'Attach files' on any task. Each file is stored privately, isolated from other workspaces, and download links are short-lived (5 minutes).

File size and total storage limits depend on your workspace's plan. If you can't upload, your admin may have hit the plan storage cap.

comments.title: Comments
comments.body:
Every task has a comments thread for collaboration. Comments support file attachments and @mentions. You can edit your own comments within 15 minutes of posting; after that they're locked.

Delete works the same way — within 15 minutes you can remove your own comment; after that, only an admin can hide it.

mentions.title: @mentions
mentions.body:
Type @ in any comment to mention a teammate. They get an in-app notification and an email (subject to their preferences). Mentions resolve by display name; if two people share a name, hover the suggestion to see their full identity.

Mentions are scoped to your workspace — you can't mention someone outside it.

reassignment.title: Asking to be reassigned
reassignment.body:
If a task lands on you that should belong to someone else, click 'Request reassignment' from the task page. Pick a target teammate and explain why.

The original assigner sees your request and either accepts (the task moves to the new person) or declines (it stays with you). Either way you get a notification.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body:
The bell icon in the header shows your unread notifications. Click to see the full list. Sources include: task assignments, status changes, comment mentions, broadcasts, and approaching deadlines.

Fine-tune what you receive under Settings → Notifications. Each notification type has separate in-app and email toggles.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.body:
My profile in the sidebar lets you update your display name, avatar, date of birth, address, emergency contact, and upload an ID card / CV / certificates.

Organizational fields — your role, department, team membership — are managed by your admin or HR. If something looks wrong there, ask them to update it.

leave.title: Leave (planned absence)
leave.body:
If you have an upcoming planned absence, set your leave dates in your profile. Q Task Manager will:

• Send you a reminder 3 business days before the start.

• Block new task assignments to you during the leave window.

• Surface your leave status to your manager so they can plan.
